resolved.title: Routing hot-reload after saving event_routing.json5 calls a method that does not exist on RoutingTable — reload never happens
resolved.impact: User edits routing rules via the management UI, save succeeds, but the in-memory routing table keeps the OLD rules until process restart. Example: user adds a rule routing signal_approved to a new BA supervisor, believes it is live, and trades for weeks with signals still following the old (or no) route — exactly the class of silent, delayed financial loss reported. Violates the project's core 'no restart required' principle.
resolved.fix: Replace both call sites with `_routing_table.load(cfg_path)` (which sets _path and swaps rules atomically), or add a `load_rules_from_file = load` method to RoutingTable. Remove the bare `except Exception: pass` at api.py:3592-3593 and surface reload errors in the response / return non-2xx.

resolved.title: Calculation-block failures never reach the snapshot errors channel — error dict is embedded as the calculation result and the cycle proceeds
resolved.impact: A calc script that starts throwing (e.g. after a tool output shape changes, or a rare None/empty-list edge on quiet market days) does NOT invalidate the snapshot. The LLM receives '"calculations": {"global": {"risk_calc": {"error": "KeyError: ...", "traceback": ...}}}' instead of the computed risk/level numbers and still makes a trade decision — exactly the rare, random-seeming financial-loss pattern, and a direct violation of the owner's fail-closed guard rule. Also: subsequent script blocks receive the error dict via `{**tool_results_by_output_key, **calc_results_by_id}` (line 677) and silently miscompute.
resolved.fix: Give _execute_calculation_blocks an errors return channel: on exception (both in _calc_script and the handler try at 685-687), append f"{block_id}:calculation_failed:{tb}" to a list returned to _build_analysis_snapshot_inner, which extends `errors`. Do not store error dicts as calculation results (or store them AND fail the snapshot).

resolved.title: _handle_close_request stringifies TradeResult and hardcodes success=True, so close status/pnl/close_price never reach the agent or the order book
resolved.impact: Every agent-initiated close: (1) result_status is "UNKNOWN", so the tool's `result_status == "CLOSED"` branch (close_position.py:142) never runs — the order book entry is never marked CLOSED/AGENT_CLOSED with pnl and close_price; (2) the partial-close branch (`result_status == "OPEN"`, line 158) never adjusts remaining units; (3) `success = result_status != "REJECTED"` is True even when the broker rejected the close — the agent believes the position is flat while it keeps running at the broker, accruing losses. The entry is later closed by the sync loop as SYNC_DETECTED, erasing agent attribution and the agent's close reasoning — corrupting OptimizationAgent training data. Exactly the reported class of rare, random-seeming losses.
resolved.fix: Mirror the order handler: `if hasattr(result, "model_dump"): result_dict = result.model_dump(mode="json")`. Additionally map field names the consumer expects: consumer reads `close_price` and `remaining_units` but TradeResult has `fill_price` and no remaining_units — either add explicit keys (`status`, `close_price` from fill_price, `pnl`, `order_id` from broker_order_id) or change the tool to read TradeResult field names. Do NOT hardcode success; derive it from TradeResult.status.

resolved.title: _handle_modify_request stringifies TradeResult — broker-rejected SL/TP modifications are recorded as applied in the order book
resolved.impact: If the broker rejects or partially applies an SL/TP change (invalid distance, closed market, position already gone), the local order book still records the new protective stop. The agent and risk logic believe a tighter stop-loss exists when it does not — position runs unprotected at the broker until an SL that was never placed 'mysteriously' fails to trigger. Direct financial-loss vector, invisible until it hits.
resolved.fix: Use `result.model_dump(mode="json")` for TradeResult (same as _handle_order_request) so `status` reaches the consumer; in modify_order.py only persist SL/TP when the returned status confirms the modification (and ideally read back the broker's applied values).

resolved.title: Batch/emergency close reads pos["position_id"] but POSITIONS_RESPONSE positions carry "broker_position_id" — causes empty ID and infinite recursion; close-all-for-pair never closes anything
resolved.impact: The documented emergency `position_id='0'` (close ALL) and close-by-pair paths never close a single position; instead they loop (POSITIONS_REQUEST every recursion) until Python recursion limit or repeated 20-30s bus timeouts abort the tool. In a drawdown emergency the agent's 'close everything' command silently does nothing — worst-case loss scenario.
resolved.fix: Read `pos.get("broker_position_id", "")` (or have _handle_positions_request emit a `position_id` alias); additionally guard the recursion: raise instead of falling through to the by-pair branch when a recursive call has an empty ID.

resolved.title: Emergency close-all (position_id='0') targets adapter member '{BROKER}-ALL___-AD-ADPT' which is never registered — request silently dropped, kill-switch never works
resolved.impact: The documented emergency close-ALL path (`position_id='0' closes ALL positions across ALL pairs (emergency)`) always hangs 20s and raises asyncio.TimeoutError; zero positions are closed at exactly the moment an agent decides to emergency-flatten the account. Even if delivery worked, finding #1 (wrong position_id key) would still break it.
resolved.fix: Route the ALL-pairs request to any registered adapter of that broker (e.g. pick one of the broker's registered pair members), or register each adapter additionally under the '{BROKER}-ALL___-AD-ADPT' id in start_background_tasks.

resolved.title: Batch close reads wrong payload key 'position_id' — producer emits 'broker_position_id' — causing empty IDs and infinite recursion
resolved.impact: "Close all positions for pair X" never closes anything. With position_id="" the recursive call falls into `if not position_id:` (line 85), pair_arg resolves to context.pair, and the pair-batch branch re-fetches the SAME positions and recurses again with empty IDs — unbounded async recursion that hammers the broker positions endpoint on every level until RecursionError. In live trading an agent trying to flatten exposure (e.g. before news) leaves all positions open while the tool errors out — exactly the class of rare, loss-producing failure reported.
resolved.fix: Use `pos.get("broker_position_id", "")` at lines 73 and 101, and skip (or error on) positions whose ID is empty instead of recursing into the pair branch.

resolved.title: Blocking synchronous HTTP requests to mql5.com executed inside async tool on the shared event loop — freezes the entire trading system for up to minutes
resolved.impact: A busy news window (e.g. NFP day: 10+ matching events) means 10+ sequential HTTPS round-trips to mql5.com, each with a 30s timeout — worst case >5 minutes during which the WHOLE process is frozen: no candle events dispatched, no POSITIONS/ORDER responses processed, stop-loss management and pending bus_request futures all time out. This happens precisely at high-impact news times, producing exactly the random-seeming losses after weeks of live trading.
resolved.fix: Wrap the whole blocking pipeline in `await asyncio.to_thread(create_events_markdown, ...)` (same for find_event_ids and the read_text), or convert the lib to httpx.AsyncClient with concurrent fetches and a hard overall deadline.

resolved.title: Batch close reads pos.get("position_id") but POSITIONS_RESPONSE carries "broker_position_id" — batch/emergency closes send empty IDs
resolved.impact: "Close all positions for a pair" and the emergency close-ALL path iterate positions but issue closes with an empty position ID; OANDA close_position raises 'position not found' — nothing is closed while the tool loops through and reports per-position results. In a margin emergency, positions stay open.
resolved.fix: Read `pos.get("broker_position_id", "")` in both loops (lines 73 and 101), or reshape the producer payload once in _handle_positions_request.

resolved.title: ORDER_MODIFY_REQUEST payload lacks the schema-required "entry_id" — bus validation rejects every SL/TP modification
resolved.impact: Agents can never adjust a stop-loss or take-profit at the broker. An LLM decision to tighten a stop (e.g. move to break-even) silently fails as a tool error; the position keeps its original SL and later loses the full original risk — exactly the class of rare, random-seeming live loss described by the owner.
resolved.fix: Either add "entry_id" to the modify_order.py payload (it isn't known there — the tool works with broker position_id), or correct event_schemas.json5 to require "position_id" for order_modify_request instead of "entry_id".

resolved.title: _write_system_config overwrites the entire production system.json5 with a modules-only stub, destroying agents/snapshot_profiles/event_composers config
resolved.impact: Re-running the setup wizard on an existing installation (e.g. to add one broker) silently wipes every agent definition, tuned system prompt, snapshot profile, session filter and EventComposer config. The system then starts from config.default.json5 fallbacks — trading behavior changes drastically with no error, or the system refuses to trade at all.
resolved.fix: Load the existing system.json5, deep-update only modules.llm/modules.broker, and re-serialize (or patch the modules block textually). At minimum, write a timestamped backup of system.json5 before overwriting and warn loudly.

resolved.title: Close-result consumer reads 'close_price', 'order_id', 'remaining_units' — producer TradeResult has none of these keys (close fill price is in 'fill_price')
resolved.impact: Every agent-initiated close persists `close_price = NULL` in the order book and returns close_price/order_id/remaining_units = null to the agent. Weeks of trades have no recorded exit price; P&L-per-pip analytics, the OptimizationAgent's inputs and any slippage detection silently operate on missing data — subtle, loss-shaping feedback corruption.
resolved.fix: Read `response.get("fill_price")` for the close price (both in the repo update at line 149 and the return dict), use `response.get("broker_order_id")` for order_id, and drop the nonexistent remaining_units key (or compute it locally).

resolved.title: Package import swallows routing-table reload failure with bare except/pass — disk and in-memory routing silently diverge
resolved.impact: After importing a package containing routing rules, imported agents' events (analysis_result → broker agent, etc.) are routed by stale rules: signals go nowhere or to the wrong agent. No error anywhere; violates the project's no-restart hot-reload guarantee silently.
resolved.fix: Report the failure like save_config_file does (routing_reload_error in the response / non-2xx), and log it; ideally validate the routing rules before writing the file.

resolved.title: ORDER_MODIFY_RESULT published without schema-required "entry_id" — response is rejected by bus validation, requester times out
resolved.impact: Even after the request-side schema defect is fixed, every modify response dies at publish time; modify_order waits the full 20 s timeout and errors, and the broker-side change (which DID execute at line 252) is invisible to the caller — local order book SL/TP diverges from the broker.
resolved.fix: Include entry_id (echo it from the request payload) or relax the order_modify_result schema; serialize TradeResult via model_dump(mode="json").

resolved.title: save_trade/get_trades/_row_to_trade_result and the trades table are dead legacy code (superseded by order_book_entries) in both adapters
resolved.impact: ~130 duplicated lines of unmaintained money-shaped code across two adapters; the PG DDL for trades (postgresql.py:73-92) is also dead. Anyone reactivating it inherits the pnl-truthiness bug (next finding).
resolved.fix: Delete save_trade, get_trades, _row_to_trade_result from both adapters, the trades DDL from postgresql.py, TRADES_TABLE from base.py, and the trades bootstrap check (sqlite.py:97-104 keeps meaning as a 001 marker — replace with a different 001 marker such as agent_decisions).

resolved.title: IndicatorToolset (the entire indicator_tools.py module) is never instantiated anywhere — it is a dead, divergent duplicate of CalculateIndicatorTool
resolved.impact: Two divergent DXY implementations: agents get a raw index float with no direction/correlation and no timestamps despite the tool description promising both; maintenance changes to one path won't reach the other. Dead code with a hidden protocol (`_pair_closes`) invites someone to 'fix' the wrong copy.
resolved.fix: Delete openforexai/data/indicator_tools.py and its __init__ export; move the direction/correlation logic (timestamp-aligned) into _compute_dxy or make _compute_dxy call the plugin properly with pair candles passed as an explicit argument instead of instance mutation.

resolved.title: IndicatorToolset is a dead, divergent twin of the calculate_indicator tool — with a different (also broken differently) DXY implementation

resolved.title: trigger_sync() is a ~120-line copy of the _sync_loop body that has already diverged: it no longer updates stop_loss/take_profit and never publishes discrepancy events
resolved.impact: A manual sync (trigger_sync tool / POSITIONS_REQUEST with trigger_sync=true) reconciles positions but silently skips SL/TP reconciliation, so broker-side SL changes are only picked up by the periodic loop; the two 'identical' sync paths keep drifting further apart with each edit.
resolved.fix: Extract one _sync_pair(pair, event_bus, emit_events: bool) coroutine used by both _sync_loop and trigger_sync; restore SL/TP updates in the shared path.
resolved.resolved_in: ad-hoc fix (2026-07-07): extracted shared _sync_pair() for _sync_loop/trigger_sync, restored SL/TP + discrepancy events

resolved.title: stop() only flips _running: a sleeping timer loop still fires one more full trade cycle, and stop() during config-wait is silently overridden by `self._running = True`
resolved.impact: 1) Disabling a timer agent via config save: the timer completes its sleep (up to interval seconds, e.g. 300 s) and executes one more full LLM+broker cycle — a trade placed by an agent the operator believes is stopped. 2) stop() issued while the agent is still in _wait_for_config: line 153 sets _running=True afterwards and the agent runs forever; since the API already unregistered its bus queue, the message loop starves but the timer loop keeps analysing/trading indefinitely — an invisible orphan trader. 3) If runtime is paused, `wait_until_resumed()` loops forever regardless of _running, so stop() never completes the loops.
resolved.fix: Make stop() cancel the loops: keep references to the TaskGroup tasks (or the start() task) and cancel them in stop(); guard start() phase 4 with `if not self._running_requested_stop`. In the timer loop, re-check `self._running` immediately after the sleep and inside wait_until_resumed (pass a predicate or use an asyncio.Event set by stop()).
resolved.resolved_in: ad-hoc fix (2026-07-07): stop() now tracks loop task refs and cancels them; guards Phase 4 with _stop_requested

resolved.title: Timer-triggered and agent_query-triggered cycles bypass _run_lock, so two cycles can run concurrently and corrupt the shared ToolContext (pair/extra)
resolved.impact: An agent_query cycle (UI chat) or timer cycle overlapping a management-API execute cycle or each other: cycle A sets context.pair, cycle B overwrites it, A's finally restores the pre-A value while B is still mid-flight — B's tools (including auto_place_order sizing/price lookups) then run against the wrong instrument. For the ALL___ BA, that is an order placed on the wrong pair — rare, random-seeming, only when triggers coincide.
resolved.fix: Acquire self._run_lock around every _run_cycle invocation (timer loop and agent_query branch), or stop mutating the shared ToolContext and pass a per-cycle context object into the dispatcher instead.
resolved.resolved_in: ad-hoc fix (2026-07-07): timer loop and agent_query branch now serialize on self._run_lock (skip-if-busy for timer, wait for agent_query)

resolved.title: Sync loop uses one stale broker_positions snapshot against later-fetched local state — falsely closes just-opened positions and ghost-imports just-closed ones
resolved.impact: (a) A position opened by an agent after the snapshot but before the pair's local_open fetch appears locally with a broker_order_id absent from stale broker_ids → marked CLOSED/SYNC_DETECTED with no pnl (get_closed_trade_result finds an open trade); next cycle re-imports it as an unattributed 'broker_sync' duplicate — agent context, reasoning and confidence lost, P&L attribution corrupted. (b) A position closed by an agent after the snapshot is still in broker_positions but gone from local_open → ghost-imported as a new OPEN entry, then closed again next cycle as SYNC_DETECTED, pulling realized pnl a second time → duplicate closed-trade records and double-counted P&L. Both are rare (sub-second to multi-second window, widened by slow repo ops for later pairs in sorted order) — precisely the random-seeming defects after weeks of trading.
resolved.fix: Fetch broker positions and local entries atomically per pair (or re-fetch broker positions immediately before the discrepancy pass), add an opened_at/requested_at grace period (e.g. skip entries with last update < 2*sync_interval) before declaring a broker-side close, and re-verify with a fresh get_open_positions before importing or closing.
resolved.resolved_in: ad-hoc fix (2026-07-07): _sync_pair fetches broker positions+local entries atomically per pair, adds grace period + fresh re-verify before declaring a close

resolved.title: Calculation blocks with unknown/non-'script' type are silently skipped — no error, snapshot proceeds without their output
resolved.impact: A typo'd or legacy `type` in a profile's calculation_blocks (e.g. "scripts", "Script") makes that calculation vanish from every live snapshot with zero diagnostics; the LLM decides without the intended risk/level data for weeks — silent degraded decisions, no crash.
resolved.fix: Treat unknown calc_type as a hard error: append f"{block_id}:unknown_calculation_type:{calc_type}" to an errors channel returned to the caller (see previous finding) so the agent skips the cycle.
resolved.resolved_in: ad-hoc fix (2026-07-07): unknown calc_type now hard-errors into the errors channel instead of silent skip

resolved.title: Failed transform stores the RAW untransformed tool output under output_key, feeding wrong-shaped data to calc blocks, assembly script, and (on API execute paths) the LLM
resolved.impact: Raw broker candle dicts (Decimal-typed, unnormalized keys) flow into calc scripts and the decision payload as if they were the normalized form; on the manual BA execute path a trade decision runs on the poisoned snapshot despite recorded validation errors.
resolved.fix: On transform failure set a sentinel (do NOT write raw_result into transformed_outputs / block["result"]); include transform_error in the has_error meta; make api.py BA/generic execute paths gate on validation_errors like the AA path (api.py:583); stop discarding errors at agent.py:889.
resolved.resolved_in: ad-hoc fix (2026-07-07): failed transform now stores None sentinel (never raw_result); has_error meta fixed; BA/generic api.py execute paths now gate on validation_errors like AA; fallback snapshot errors no longer discarded

resolved.title: Calc block id defaults to calc_type — multiple id-less 'script' blocks all get id 'script' and silently overwrite each other
resolved.impact: The first calculation's output disappears from the snapshot with no error — the LLM trades on half the intended calculations, and a later script referencing the shared key reads the wrong block's result. Classic weeks-later silent-loss defect triggered by adding a second unnamed script block.
resolved.fix: Default block_id to f"{calc_type}_{index+1}" and hard-error (errors channel) on duplicate calc ids and on calc ids colliding with tool output_keys.
resolved.resolved_in: ad-hoc fix (2026-07-07): calc block id defaults to f"{calc_type}_{index+1}"; duplicate ids and id/tool-output_key collisions now hard-error

resolved.title: 8 of 10 analysis-snapshot tests fail: build_analysis_snapshot/preview_snapshot_tool_block no longer accept data_container kwarg and ToolContext dropped data_container — the LLM decision-input pipeline is effectively untested
resolved.impact: Snapshot tool blocks, calculation blocks, assembly transforms, SHORT_TF/LONG_TF placeholder resolution, and CalculateIndicatorTool — everything that assembles the market data the LLM trades on — has no running coverage. Per project memory, calculation_blocks is the ONLY snapshot path, so a regression here alters every trade decision unnoticed.
resolved.fix: Port the stubs to the new interface (event_bus-based CANDLES_REQUEST responder or the repository/broker kwargs) and re-enable all 8 tests.
resolved.resolved_in: ad-hoc fix (2026-07-07): rewrote test_analysis_snapshot.py for the event_bus/CANDLES_REQUEST interface (data_container kwarg removed); all 9 tests pass

resolved.title: OrderStatus is used but never imported — NameError silently kills broker reconciliation of PENDING/OPEN order-book entries
resolved.impact: The /orderbook reconcile path can never confirm a PENDING entry as OPEN nor transition an OPEN entry to CLOSED. Only the sub-case where the entry is already CLOSED (line 1078 `if status_value != "CLOSED"` skips the OrderStatus reference) works, i.e. pnl refresh of already-closed entries — making the defect look like it partially works. Order book shown in the UI stays stale (unconfirmed/phantom-open positions), sync_confirmed/confirmed_by_broker never set via this path, and operators make trading decisions against a wrong position book.
resolved.fix: Add `from openforexai.models.trade import OrderStatus` to the module imports (and consider `CloseReason` for parity with base.py). Add a regression test that exercises _reconcile_order_book_entries_with_broker with a PENDING entry.
resolved.resolved_in: ad-hoc fix (2026-07-07): added missing OrderStatus import; also fixed 2 broken get_closed_trade_result(sync_key=...) callers left over from an earlier dead_code removal (api.py, scripts/backfill_order_results.py)

resolved.title: SPA catch-all route has no path containment check — unauthenticated path traversal can serve arbitrary files (including system.json5 with secrets)
resolved.impact: Any network client that can reach the management port can read arbitrary files under (and above) ui/dist — including config/system.json5, broker module configs with API keys/passwords, the SQLite DB, and .env — without the X-API-Key header. Direct credential/broker-account compromise vector.
resolved.fix: Resolve and contain: `target = (_ui_dist / full_path).resolve(); try: target.relative_to(_ui_dist.resolve()) except ValueError: return index.html`. Or serve via Starlette StaticFiles (which performs this check) on an http-only sub-path.
resolved.resolved_in: ad-hoc fix (2026-07-07): SPA catch-all now resolves + containment-checks the target path against ui/dist before serving, falls back to index.html on traversal

resolved.title: _run_runtime_agent / _run_runtime_ec swallow all startup exceptions — a hot-enabled agent that crashes dies silently while remaining registered as active
resolved.impact: Operator enables an agent via the UI; save returns {"started": 1}; the agent's start() raises (bad LLM config, broker missing, etc.) and the exception vanishes. The agent appears in /composers and _active_agents lookups but processes nothing — positions it was supposed to manage (e.g. a broker agent handling exits) are silently unmanaged for weeks. Exactly the reported class of loss.
resolved.fix: Log the exception with agent_id, emit a monitoring event (e.g. system_error pinned), and remove the instance from _active_agents/_runtime_agents (+ unregister from bus) so the failure is visible and a subsequent save retries the start.
resolved.resolved_in: ad-hoc fix (2026-07-07): _run_runtime_agent/_run_runtime_ec now log+monitor+unregister on startup crash instead of silently swallowing the exception while staying registered as active

resolved.title: Running EventComposers never receive updated config after PUT /config/system — only agents get a config refresh
resolved.impact: Editing a running EC's script/triggers/tool_config in system.json5 and saving reports "saved" but the live EC keeps executing the OLD script indefinitely (e.g. an updated guard threshold or risk filter). Directly violates the project's core 'Kein Neustart erforderlich' rule and produces exactly the weeks-later random-loss pattern: operator believes new logic is live.
resolved.fix: Add a _trigger_ec_config_refresh() that publishes EC_CONFIG_REQUESTED (payload {"ec_id": id}) for every enabled+registered EC, and call it from _apply_runtime_composer_changes (and thus from both PUT /config/system and the package import path).
resolved.resolved_in: ad-hoc fix (2026-07-07): added _trigger_ec_config_refresh() (mirrors agent-side refresh), called from _apply_runtime_composer_changes so running ECs get a live EC_CONFIG_REQUESTED after PUT /config/system
